questions.prompt: How is GitHub best described, relative to Git?

options.text: It is the version-control tool that replaces Git
It is a service that hosts Git repositories and adds collaboration features
It is a different command-line program you install instead of Git
It is a text editor for writing commits

questions.explanation: GitHub hosts Git repositories and layers on collaboration features (PRs, issues, reviews). Git is the underlying version-control tool.

questions.prompt: Over HTTPS, what do you use to authenticate Git operations with GitHub?

options.text: A Personal Access Token (or a credential manager that stores it)

questions.explanation: GitHub removed account-password authentication for Git operations in 2021. Over HTTPS you supply a Personal Access Token, often stored by a credential manager.

questions.prompt: Which statements about GitHub authentication are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: SSH authentication uses a key pair
You add the public key to GitHub, keeping the private key secret
A Personal Access Token can stand in for a password over HTTPS
You should commit your token into the repository for convenience

questions.explanation: SSH uses a key pair (public on GitHub, private secret), and a PAT replaces a password over HTTPS. Committing a token exposes it — never do that.

questions.prompt: To connect a local repository to a GitHub remote named origin, run: git remote ___ origin <url>
questions.explanation: git remote add origin <url> registers the GitHub URL under the name origin so you can push and pull.

questions.prompt: You clone over HTTPS and enter your GitHub account password when prompted, but it fails. Why?

options.text: GitHub removed password authentication for Git operations; use a token or SSH
You must be on the same network as GitHub
Passwords only work for git pull, not git clone

questions.explanation: Since 2021, account passwords aren't accepted for Git operations. The prompt says 'Password' but expects a Personal Access Token (or use SSH keys).

questions.prompt: Match each item to its role.

pairs.right: Key pair; public key on GitHub
Link a local repo to a remote
Download a repo and set up origin

questions.explanation: A PAT authenticates HTTPS, SSH uses key pairs, remote add links a remote, and clone copies a repo while configuring origin.
